entities.summary:
Conrad of Vechta was a key figure in the ecclesiastical politics of the Holy Roman Empire during the 15th century. As Bishop of Verden (1400–1402/1407), he played a crucial role in the conflict between the Archbishop of Cologne and the Bishop of Bremen.

Conrad's appointment as Archbishop of Prague (1413–1421) marked a significant shift in the political landscape of the region, as he sought to assert the authority of the Holy Roman Emperor over the Bohemian territories.

As Master of the Mint (1401–1403) and Chancellor (1405–1412) of the Kingdom of Bohemia, Conrad oversaw the development of the mint's currency and facilitated trade between the kingdom and other European powers.


Conrad of Vechta's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Holy Roman Empire on the politics and culture of the region, as well as the development of the Bohemian crown jewels.
